analysis.title: GS Pasquariello - markets macro 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 made a tentative break above the congestion zone around 7700 and keeps absorbing pressure from adjacent asset classes, most notably a rise in global bond yields.

The rally is extremely narrow within a bifurcated market. US mega cap tech has led, while rate-sensitive and cyclical sectors have been weak. Per Brian Garrett, nearly half of S&P names had a negative beta to the index over the summer.
The primary bull trend remains intact for both S&P and NDX, per big-picture chart work.
The trading community carries a conspicuously low level of length, even though the tape made higher highs as recently as Tuesday.
Q3 earnings growth expectation is 28% y/y, which Pasquariello is not inclined to fight as the reporting period starts.
Higher rates are becoming a bigger risk to both sovereigns and corporates.
US mega cap tech is shouldering more of the load, which raises concentration risk.
Q4 seasonals are friendlier, but Pasquariello expects the midterms to bring a dose of volatility.

Bottom line: it is a bull market, but short-term risk/reward is unclear, so he advises observing the speed limit. He sees no reason to leave the US and Japan, and still pairs a long equity position with a paid rates position, which plays on nominal growth staying higher for longer.

Tech and energy stocks have moved together. Q3 earnings growth is expected at +64% y/y for tech and +122% for energy. A 50/50 tech/energy composite was up in 10 of the past 11 years, with an average annual return of 18.7% and a Sharpe of 1.2.
